key_insight: Native-defect stability in MnSe depends on crystal structure, growth conditions and magnetic order, while 3% defects largely preserve the peak spin splitting studied in A-type wurtzite MnSe.
engineering_relevance: Growth chemistry offers a route to favor particular defects, with Mn vacancies dominant across most of the rock-salt growth window and consistent with p-type conduction.
method: DFT with linear-response Hubbard U for neutral Mn and Se vacancies and both antisites.
Formation-energy comparison across Se-rich and Mn-rich limits in rock-salt and wurtzite MnSe.
Magnetic-order comparison and band unfolding to assess defect-induced spin-splitting changes.
evidence_signal: The rock-salt Mn vacancy costs 0.92 eV at the Se-rich limit; wurtzite stripe order lies 14 meV per formula unit below A-type order, whose approximately 230 meV peak splitting remains within 8% analysis scatter at 3% defects.
watch_item: DFT+U incorrectly favors wurtzite over rock salt, wurtzite magnetic order remains experimentally unmeasured, and band-edge spin splitting is unresolved.
paper_title: Native point defects in rock-salt and wurtzite MnSe: formation energies across the growth window and spin splitting in the A-type order
